extracted.intended_audience: licensees, spectrum lessees, wireless carriers, FCC applicants, and communications counsel (parties filing spectrum leasing notifications/applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for entering, notifying, obtaining consent for, and operating under spectrum leasing arrangements (spectrum manager and de facto transfer; long-term and short-term), including special requirements for Contraband Interdiction Systems. Covers who is responsible for regulatory obligations and how applications/notifications are processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and ULS reflection of qualifying notifications (immediate processing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided that the notification establishes that the proposed spectrum manager leasing arrangement meets all of the requisite elements to qualify for these immediate processing procedures, ULS will reflect that the notification has been accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed electronically, acceptance will be reflected in ULS on the next business day after filing; if filed manually, on the next business day after necessary data are entered into ULS. Once accepted and reflected in ULS, the spectrum lessee may commence operations under the arrangement, consistent with the term of the arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and reconsideration for notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: A notification filed pursuant to these immediate processing procedures will be placed on an informational public notice on a weekly basis once accepted, and is subject to reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.933(a) for public notice and §§ 1.106(f), 1.108, 1.113 for reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of a spectrum manager leasing arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: The spectrum manager leasing arrangement will be deemed effective in the Commission's records, and for purposes of the application of the rules set forth in this section, as of the beginning date of the term as specified in the spectrum leasing notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The effective date is the beginning date specified in the notification; Commission records reflect that date for rule application purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission termination authority for spectrum manager leasing arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission retains the right to investigate and terminate any spectrum manager leasing arrangement if it determines, post-notification, that the arrangement constitutes an unauthorized transfer of de facto control of the leased spectrum, is otherwise in violation of the rules in this chapter, or raises foreign ownership, competitive, or other public interest concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information concerning any such termination will be placed on public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expiration, extension, and early termination notification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A spectrum leasing arrangement entered into pursuant to this section will expire on the termination date set forth in the notification unless extended or terminated earlier; extensions and early terminations have specified notification timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To extend beyond initial term, licensee must notify Commission in advance pursuant to the general or immediate procedures (if general procedures apply, notify at least 21 days in advance). If terminated earlier than the date set forth, licensee must file notification no later than 10 days after early termination indicating the date. Commission will place information concerning extensions or early terminations on public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of a spectrum leasing arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: The spectrum lessee may assign its spectrum leasing arrangement to another entity provided that the licensee has agreed to such an assignment, is in privity with the assignee, and notifies the Commission before consummation pursuant to applicable notification procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-substantial (pro forma) assignments falling within § 1.948(c)(1), licensee must file notification with FCC Form 608 and updates of ownership information within 30 days of completion. Commission places assignment information on public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of control of a spectrum lessee: pre-consummation notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee must notify the Commission of any transfer of control of a spectrum lessee before the consummation of the transfer of control, pursuant to the applicable notification procedures of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-substantial (pro forma) transfers within § 1.948(c)(1), parties must file notification with FCC Form 608 and provide ownership updates within 30 days of completion; Commission places related information on public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation or automatic cancellation consequences and STA consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: If an authorization held by a licensee that has a spectrum leasing arrangement is revoked or cancelled, the spectrum lessee must terminate its operations no later than the date the licensee ceases to have authority to operate under the license, except as otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission will consider a request by the spectrum lessee for special temporary authority (see § 1.931) to allow transition of users to minimize service disruption. The former spectrum lessee does not receive any preference over other parties when seeking the revoked or cancelled license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subleasing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A spectrum lessee may sublease the leased spectrum usage rights subject to the licensee's consent and the licensee's establishment of privity with the spectrum sublessee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The licensee must submit a notification regarding the subleasing arrangement in accordance with applicable notification procedures. In long-term contexts, once approved the sublessee becomes primarily responsible for compliance with Commission rules and policies; written consent from the licensee must be included in the application for subleasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal of a spectrum leasing arrangement contingent on license renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the term of a spectrum leasing arrangement may not be longer than the term of a license authorization, an arrangement whose term continues to the end of the current license term may, contingent on the Commission's grant of license renewal, be renewed to extend into the term of the renewed license authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission must be notified of the renewal of the spectrum leasing arrangement at the same time the licensee submits its application for license renewal (see § 1.949). The spectrum lessee may operate under the extended term until the Commission makes a final determination on the license renewal and the extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community notification requirement for Contraband Interdiction Systems (CIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: 10 days prior to deploying a Contraband Interdiction System that prevents communications to or from mobile devices, a lessee must notify the community in which the correctional facility is located.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must include a description of system intent, scheduled start date, and facility location; must be tailored to reach the community immediately adjacent to the facility through local TV, radio, Internet news sources, or community groups as appropriate. No notification required for brief tests prior to deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and term limit for long-term de facto transfer leasing arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'long-term' de facto transfer leasing arrangement has an individual term, or series of combined terms, of more than one year; the term may be no longer than the term of the license authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee retains de jure control while de facto control transfers to the lessee for the arrangement duration, subject to prior Commission consent under application procedures in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee rights and responsibilities under long-term de facto transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided, the licensee is relieved of primary and direct responsibility for ensuring that the spectrum lessee's operations comply with the Communications Act and Commission rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee remains responsible for its own violations, including those related to the leasing arrangement, and for ongoing violations or egregious behavior of which it has knowledge or should have knowledge. Licensee must retain a copy of the spectrum leasing agreement and make it available upon Commission request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrum lessee rights and responsibilities under long-term de facto transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The spectrum lessee assumes primary responsibility for complying with the Communications Act and applicable Commission policies and rules and is granted an instrument of authorization bringing it within scope of Commission's direct forfeiture provisions under section 503(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessee is responsible for interacting with the Commission regarding leased spectrum and making all related filings (e.g., applications/notifications, Environmental Assessment materials, required reports, information for international/IRAC coordination). Lessee must maintain accurate information on file per § 1.65 and retain a copy of the agreement for Commission requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of interference and RF safety rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The interference and radiofrequency (RF) safety rules applicable to use of the spectrum by the licensee as a condition of its license authorization also apply to the use of the spectrum leased by the spectrum lessee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessee operations must comply with same interference and RF safety obligations as the licensee's authorized use.

rubrics_metrics.name: General eligibility and qualification requirements for spectrum lessee
rubrics_metrics.description: The spectrum lessee must meet the same eligibility and qualification requirements that are applicable to the licensee under its license authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes foreign ownership eligibility requirements (sections 310(a), 310(b) of the Communications Act), character qualifications, and prohibition on persons subject to denial of Federal benefits under the Anti-Drug Abuse Act of 1988 (see § 1.2001 et seq.). Exception: lessee entering arrangement involving a Public Safety Radio Services licensee need not comply with certain eligibility requirements so long as lessee provides communications in support of public safety operations (§ 90.523(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use restrictions apply to spectrum lessee
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent the licensee is restricted from using the licensed spectrum to offer particular services under its authorization, those use restrictions apply to the spectrum lessee as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessee cannot use the leased spectrum for services prohibited by the license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated entity / entrepreneur rules and unjust enrichment obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee that holds a license pursuant to small business and/or entrepreneur provisions and continues to be subject to unjust enrichment requirements and/or transfer restrictions may enter into a long-term de facto transfer leasing arrangement under streamlined processing, subject to any applicable unjust enrichment payment obligations and/or transfer restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amount of any unjust enrichment payment will be determined by the Commission as part of its review using the same rules as license assignment/transfer of control; if arrangement involves only part of license area or bandwidth, unjust enrichment is apportioned as though partitioning/disaggregation. No reduction in payment obligation if arrangement ends prior to five years of license term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction/performance requirements remain license condition and non-delegable
rubrics_metrics.description: Any performance or build-out requirement applicable under a license authorization always remains a condition of the license, and the legal responsibility for meeting such obligation is not delegable to the spectrum lessee(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee may attribute lessee build-out or performance activities for compliance purposes; if licensee relies on lessee and lessee fails to act, Commission will enforce applicable obligations against licensee. Licensee is accountable for rules concerning discontinuance of operation regardless of reliance on lessee activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory classification parity and exception
rubrics_metrics.description: If regulatory status of the licensee (e.g., common carrier or non-common carrier) is prescribed by rule, the regulatory status of the spectrum lessee is prescribed the same manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: § 20.9(a) shall not preclude a licensee in the services covered by that rule from entering into a spectrum leasing arrangement with a spectrum lessee that chooses to operate on a PMRS, private, or non-commercial basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory fees responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee remains responsible for payment of the required regulatory fees that must be paid in advance of its license term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where fees are paid annually on a per-unit basis (e.g., CMRS services), the licensee and spectrum lessee each are required to pay fees for those units associated with its respective operations (see § 1.1152).

rubrics_metrics.name: E911 obligations for lessee and CIS providers
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent the licensee is required to meet E911 obligations, the spectrum lessee is required to meet those obligations with respect to the spectrum leased insofar as the lessee's operations are encompassed within the E911 obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the spectrum lessee is a Contraband Interdiction System (CIS) provider (defined in § 1.9003), the CIS provider is responsible for compliance with § 9.10(r) regarding E911 transmission obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application filing requirements for long-term de facto transfer leasing arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must submit the application by electronic filing using ULS and FCC Form 608, and obtain Commission consent prior to consummating the transfer of de facto control, except that parties within § 1.913(d) may file either electronically or manually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications will be processed pursuant to general approval procedures or immediate approval procedures depending on qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: General approval procedural sufficiency and fee treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: To be accepted for filing under general approval procedures, the application must be sufficiently complete and contain all information and certifications requested on FCC Form 608, including those of the spectrum lessee relating to eligibility, basic qualifications, and foreign ownership, and include payment of required application fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of determining applicable application fees, the application will be treated as a transfer of control (see § 1.1102). Once accepted for filing, the application will be placed on public notice (with limited exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice placement and petitions to deny timing (general approval)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once accepted for filing, the application will be placed on public notice (except no prior public notice required for certain Private Wireless Services). Petitions to deny under section 309(d) must comply with § 1.939 and must be filed no later than 14 days following the date of the public notice listing the application as accepted for filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any petition to deny is filed and the Bureau grants the application, the Bureau will deny the petition(s) and issue a concise statement disposing of all substantive issues raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wireless Bureau timelines for review and further review process
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than 21 days following the date of the public notice listing an application as accepted for filing, the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau will affirmatively consent to the application, deny the application, or determine to subject the application to further review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications with no prior public notice required, the Bureau acts no later than 21 days following filing and payment of any required fee. If the Bureau determines to subject the application to further review, it will issue a public notice and within 90 days will either take action or provide public notice that an additional 90-day period is needed. Consent is not deemed granted until the Bureau affirmatively acts on the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate approval procedural additional qualifications (long-term)
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for immediate approval, the application must be sufficiently complete and include certifications that the following qualifications are met: (A) license does not involve spectrum in a Wireless Radio Service that may be used to provide interconnected mobile voice/data services creating geographic overlap with spectrum in which proposed lessee already holds a 10%+ direct or indirect interest and could be used to provide interconnected mobile services; (B) licensee is not a designated entity or entrepreneur subject to unjust enrichment/transfer restrictions; (C) arrangement does not require a waiver or declaratory ruling of Commission rules; (D) application does not involve a transaction in the Enhanced Competition Incentive Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These additional certifications are required on top of the general completeness, eligibility, foreign ownership, and fee requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate approval procedures for Contraband Interdiction Systems (CIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: A lessee of spectrum used in a Contraband Interdiction System qualifies for immediate approval if the application is sufficiently complete, contains all necessary information and certifications (including eligibility, basic qualifications, and foreign ownership), and does not require a waiver or declaratory ruling of any applicable Commission rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it meets the requisite elements, consent will be reflected in ULS per timing rules; consent is not deemed granted until the Bureau affirmatively acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: ULS reflection timing for immediate approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided that the application/notification establishes it meets all requisite elements to qualify for immediate procedures, ULS will reflect acceptance/consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed electronically, reflection in ULS occurs on the next business day after filing; if filed manually, on the next business day after necessary data entry. Consent/acceptance is not deemed granted until the Bureau affirmatively acts as reflected in ULS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of de facto transfer leasing arrangements after consent
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission consents to the de facto transfer leasing arrangement, the arrangement will be deemed effective in the Commission's records and for application of rules on the date set forth in the application; if consent occurs after that date, the application will become effective on the date of the Commission affirmative consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant-specified dates before Commission affirmative consent are not effective until the Bureau acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and transfer approval requirements for long-term de facto
rubrics_metrics.description: The spectrum lessee may assign its lease to another entity provided the licensee agreed, there is privity between licensee and assignee, and the assignment is approved by the Commission pursuant to the same application and approval procedures set forth in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-substantial (pro forma) assignments within § 1.948(c)(1) require notification with FCC Form 608 and ownership updates within 30 days; Commission will place assignment information on public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subleasing application content for long-term de facto transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties entering into a spectrum subleasing arrangement are required to comply with Commission rules for obtaining approval and the application must include written consent from the licensee to the proposed arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a spectrum subleasing arrangement has been approved, the sublessee becomes the party primarily responsible for compliance with Commission rules and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and term limits for short-term de facto transfer leasing arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'short-term' de facto transfer leasing arrangement has an individual or combined term of not longer than one year; term may be no longer than the term of the license authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee retains de jure control while de facto control is transferred to the lessee for the arrangement duration, and prior Commission consent is required per section procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights/responsibilities under short-term de facto same as long-term
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights and responsibilities applicable to licensee and spectrum lessee in a short-term de facto transfer leasing arrangement are the same as those under a long-term de facto transfer leasing arrangement (see § 1.9030(b) and (c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except where this section provides specific deviations for short-term arrangements (see following entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term use restrictions and regulatory classification exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use restrictions applicable to the licensee also apply to the spectrum lessee except that § 20.9(a) shall not preclude a licensee in the covered services from entering into an arrangement with a lessee that chooses to operate on a PMRS, private, or non-commercial basis, and a licensee with an authorization restricting spectrum to non-commercial uses may enter into a short-term de facto transfer leasing arrangement that allows the spectrum lessee to use the spectrum commercially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-term arrangements may permit uses otherwise restricted under license in some circumstances described here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term designated entity / unjust enrichment exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Unjust enrichment provisions (see § 1.2111) and transfer restrictions (see § 24.839) do not apply with regard to a short-term de facto transfer leasing arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-term arrangement parties are exempt from these specified obligations that apply to long-term arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term construction/performance attribution prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee is not permitted to attribute to itself the activities of its spectrum lessee when seeking to establish that performance or build-out requirements applicable to the licensee have been met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike long-term arrangements (where attribution is permitted), short-term arrangements prohibit licensing attribution for performance compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term E911 obligations allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: If E911 obligations apply to the licensee, the licensee retains the obligations with respect to leased spectrum; a spectrum lessee entering into a short-term de facto transfer leasing arrangement is not separately required to comply with such obligations in relation to the leased spectrum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if lessee is a CIS provider (see § 1.9003), the CIS provider is responsible for compliance with § 9.10(r) regarding E911 transmission obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term spectrum leasing application and immediate approval processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-term de facto transfer leasing arrangements will be processed pursuant to immediate approval procedures. Parties must file an electronic application using FCC Form 608 and obtain Commission consent prior to consummation, except parties within § 1.913(d) may file electronically or manually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be accepted for filing under immediate approval procedures, application must be sufficiently complete, contain all required information and certifications (including eligibility, basic qualifications, and foreign ownership), include required application fee, and the arrangement must not require a waiver or declaratory ruling of any applicable Commission rules. For fee purposes the application is treated as a transfer of control (§ 1.1102).

rubrics_metrics.name: ULS consent reflection and timing for short-term arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided the application establishes it meets all requisite elements to qualify for immediate approval procedures, consent to the short-term de facto transfer will be reflected in ULS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed electronically, consent reflected on next business day after filing; if filed manually, on next business day after necessary data entry. Consent not deemed granted until Bureau affirmatively acts as reflected in ULS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on using short-term procedures for longer arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee and spectrum lessee may not use the special rules and expedited procedures applicable to short-term de facto transfer leasing arrangements for arrangements that in fact will exceed one year, or that the parties reasonably expect to exceed one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must submit appropriate application under long-term rules in sufficient time prior to expiration if arrangement may continue; obtain Commission consent under long-term procedures.
